lastCompletedStory.title: Sweep GARBOARD out of the active presentation docs and reconcile the on-main issue records

openQuestions: AC3's repo-wide grep sweep still matches scripts/cam/prd.json and this very handoff.json's lastCompletedStory.title. prd.json necessarily narrates the retired product name in its own story titles/descriptions/notes (it is the PRD that specifies this very sweep), is worker-write-denied per ADR-0036, and is an ephemeral artifact git-rm'd at cam ship --finalize per ADR-0040, so that residual self-resolves at ship time, not fixable mid-branch. lastCompletedStory.title is required to carry this story's real title verbatim for traceability, and this story's own real title names the retired brand; that one-field residual clears on the NEXT story's handoff overwrite, not this one's. AC4-AC6 (the on-main CAM-331/CAM-417/CAM-421 issue-record edits) are explicitly out of scope for this worker per the story's own acceptance criteria text; they are on-main control-plane edits reserved for the orchestrator/operator.
nextStoryContext: docs/positioning.md and docs/launch-readiness.md now present the product as Gateship, citing ADR-0050; positioning.md's former section 4 (the full five-round naming battle, kill evidence, and reserves for the retired name) was rewritten to a short current-decision statement plus an alias/rename-policy subsection, with the full history left to live in the ADRs (docs/adr/) rather than re-narrated. No code, template, binary, or build script was touched (docs-only, matching ADR-0050's staged-rename doctrine). The three on-main issue-record reconciliations (CAM-331, CAM-417, CAM-421) named in this story's AC4-AC6 were deliberately NOT performed here: the story's own acceptance criteria text marks them as an orchestrator/operator on-main control-plane action, never a worker-on-branch edit, so a future story or the orchestrator should verify those three records directly against main rather than assuming this story closed them.
